title: Hucking after an offensive line regains possession
sections: Are UFA teams more likely to huck after their O-line loses and regains possession than on the opening possession of a receiving point? I will establish each team's usual opening-possession huck rate, then compare it with that team's rate after regaining the disc within a point. The comparison includes points ending in either a hold or a break.

I want to test whether recovering the disc is associated with a change in a team's deep-throwing tendency. My hypothesis is that hucks make up a larger share of passes after a regain, particularly early in the new possession. A finding of little change or less hucking would also answer the question. My observations about long points motivate the study, but the data cannot establish whether players feel tired or impatient.

An offensive coach could see whether the team's choices after a turnover match its intended approach, then identify points for film review or transition practice. An opposing coach could look for teams that attack deep soon after recovering the disc. I will show attempt counts and uncertainty so a small sample is not treated as a reliable tendency. The study measures throwing choices; it does not establish whether hucking more improves scoring.
